analysis_summary: Phase 2 deep analysis of Pretty Links 3.6.21. The IR map flagged 33 anomalies across 3 categories: missing nonce checks, missing capability checks, and flawed nonce patterns. Manual source-level analysis refuted all high-priority anomalies as false positives. Every 'flawed nonce' (check_ajax_referer with $die=false) is immediately checked for its return value with an explicit conditional, making them equivalent in effect to check_ajax_referer with $die=true. All 'guard after side-effect' flags in PrliAddonsController were the IR extractor misidentifying an early-exit validation check (isset test) as a side-effect — the actual dangerous operations come after all guards. The 'missing capability' anomalies were refuted by tracing to capability checks inside called helper methods (PrliUtils::is_authorized(), PrliUtils::is_logged_in_and_an_admin()). SQL usage is safe throughout: $wpdb->prepare(), $wpdb->insert(), and $wpdb->update() are used consistently. No subscriber-accessible, nonceless, unauthenticated paths to dangerous sinks were confirmed. The only elevated-risk pattern is the option key injection surface in dismiss_notice, which is neutralized by sanitize_key(). Overall risk is low.

negative_findings.reason: IR flagged guards as 'after side-effect at lines 58/101/124'. Actual code: line 57/100/123 is an isset() check on $_POST['plugin'] that calls wp_send_json_error() and returns on failure — this is request validation, not a dangerous side-effect. The capability checks (activate_plugins, deactivate_plugins, install_plugins) appear at lines 61/104/127 and the nonce checks (check_ajax_referer with explicit return-value test) at lines 65/108/131. All guards precede activate_plugins() at line 69, deactivate_plugins() at line 112, and Plugin_Upgrader::install() at line 177. check_ajax_referer is called with $die=false but the return value is explicitly tested: if(!check_ajax_referer(...)) { wp_send_json_error(); } — this is effective. No exploitable path.

check_ajax_referer('prli_admin_link_list_nonce', false, false) is used in a compound OR condition: if(!check_ajax_referer(...) || !PrliUtils::is_authorized()). If the nonce check fails, !false evaluates to true and wp_send_json_error() terminates execution. Effective guard. PrliUtils::is_authorized() checks manage_options capability by default. No bypass possible.

Guards appear in order: (1) POST validation at line 862, (2) PrliUtils::is_authorized() at line 866, (3) check_ajax_referer with explicit return-value test at line 870. The IR note 'guard at line 870 after side-effect at line 863' is incorrect — line 863 is wp_send_json_error() inside a validation block, not a dangerous side-effect. prli_link->create() only executes at line 896, after all three guards. Effective.

Uses check_ajax_referer('reset_pretty_link','security') without $die=false — kills execution on nonce failure. Followed by is_authorized(). $prli_link->reset($_POST['id']) uses $wpdb->prepare() with %d placeholder, so SQL injection is impossible even with non-integer input.

check_ajax_referer('validate_pretty_link','security') with default $die=true. Followed by is_authorized(). Error messages in HTML construction at line 487 come from hardcoded translation strings in $prli_link->validate(), not from user input.

check_ajax_referer('prli_create_link_nonce', false, false) at line 184 is tested: if(!check_ajax_referer(...)) { wp_send_json_error(); }. Execution terminates on failure. Followed by is_authorized() at line 190. All POST inputs sanitized before reaching prli_create_pretty_link().
check_ajax_referer('prli_tinymce_nonce', false, false) return value explicitly checked. Followed by is_authorized(). Slug sanitized with sanitize_text_field() before use.

IR flagged as missing nonce. Capability check present: requires is_admin() (manage_options) OR is_editor() (edit_others_posts). SQL uses $wpdb->prepare() with $wpdb->esc_like() on the LIKE parameter. No nonce, but restricted to admin/editor users — no subscriber escalation possible. The missing nonce is a low-severity observation (no dangerous write operation, read-only, capability-gated).
negative_findings.risk_note: Absence of nonce means any admin/editor user can be CSRF'd into triggering this endpoint, but it only returns link data already accessible to admins. Low real-world impact.

negative_findings.reason: IR flagged missing capability check. Actual code at line 168: wp_verify_nonce() with $die=true semantic (wp_die on failure). Then PrliUtils::is_authorized() check at line 178 before any option updates. Both nonce and capability checks are present and effective.
IR flagged missing capability. Actual code: wp_verify_nonce at line 228 (dies on failure), then PrliUtils::is_authorized() at line 233. Both guards in place before disconnect() is called.

IR flagged missing nonce AND missing capability AND flawed nonce. Actual code at line 1140: if(!is_post_request() || !is_logged_in_and_an_admin() || !check_ajax_referer(..., false, false)) { wp_send_json_error(); }. All three conditions are tested in a short-circuit OR; any failure sends error and terminates. The nonce with $die=false is checked for its return value. Effective triple guard.
Line 603: !is_get_request() || !is_logged_in_and_an_admin() || !check_ajax_referer(..., false, false) — combined condition; any failure throws Exception. Effective.
Line 740: !is_post_request() || !is_logged_in_and_an_admin() || !check_ajax_referer(..., false, false) — combined condition; any failure throws Exception. Effective.

IR flagged missing capability. Actual code: wp_verify_nonce at line 69 ($die semantics via empty check and die()), then is_authorized() at line 73. update_option('pl_dismiss_upgrade_header', true) is a fixed-key option with a boolean value — no injection surface even if auth were bypassed.

negative_findings.area: PrliAppController::dismiss_notice / dismiss_daily_notice / dismiss_monthly_notice (anom_3, anom_10, anom_22, anom_23, anom_24)
negative_findings.reason: Pattern: if(check_ajax_referer('prli_dismiss_notice', false, false) && isset($_POST['notice']) && is_string($_POST['notice'])) { if(!is_authorized()) { return; } update_option(...); }. The update_option() only executes when the nonce check PASSES. When nonce fails, code falls through to wp_send_json_success() without making any changes. The option key uses sanitize_key($_POST['notice']) which restricts to alphanumeric+dash+underscore — no option key injection possible. IR anom_3 (missing nonce) incorrect since nonce IS checked.

IR flagged missing nonce AND missing capability. Actual code: finish() at line 929 calls validate_request('prli_onboarding_finish') which: (1) checks is_post_request(), (2) checks is_logged_in_and_an_admin() (requires manage_options), (3) calls check_ajax_referer with explicit return-value check. All guards in place before update_option('prli_onboarding_complete', '1').

All handlers call get_request_data() first, which calls validate_request() — checking POST method, is_logged_in_and_an_admin() (manage_options), and nonce. Some handlers additionally check current_user_can('publish_posts') as redundant extra check. The admin check in validate_request() is the primary gate.

IR flagged guards as appearing after side-effects. Actual: all three handlers check is_post_request() first, then is_logged_in_and_an_admin() or current_user_can('update_plugins'), then check_ajax_referer with explicit return test. The 'side-effects' noted by IR are the initial return-on-bad-request validations at lines 65/160/200 (wp_send_json_error calls). Dangerous operations (activate_license, deactivate_license, install_plugin_silently) only execute after all guards pass.

PrliUtils::check_ajax_referer('prli-admin-popup','security') called first (uses check_ajax_referer with $die=true default — kills on failure). Then is_authorized(). Then is_valid_popup() validates the popup name against a fixed whitelist via in_array(). update_user_meta and update_option targets are constructed from whitelist-controlled keys.

Both hooked on init with auth_level:none in IR, but both require: (1) specific GET parameter flag, (2) wp_verify_nonce (effective, dies on failure), (3) is_authorized(). The wp_redirect() at line 125 redirects to PrliStripeConnect::get_stripe_connect_url($_GET['method_id']) which constructs a URL to hardcoded PRLI_STRIPE_SERVICE_URL with method_id embedded in a JWT path — not a user-controlled redirect destination. Open redirect flag (anom_31, anom_32, anom_33) refuted. Similarly for StripeConnectController redirects which redirect to admin_url() constructed paths.

wp_redirect() used instead of wp_safe_redirect(). Targets: (1) process_update_creds line 126 redirects to add_query_arg(..., admin_url('edit.php?...')), (2) process_refresh_tokens line 216 redirects to add_query_arg(..., admin_url('edit.php?...')), (3) process_disconnect line 251 redirects to add_query_arg(..., admin_url('edit.php?...')). All redirect targets are constructed from admin_url() with no user-controlled hostname component. The $_GET['stripe-action'] parameter is sanitized with sanitize_text_field() before inclusion as a query parameter value. No open redirect.
Hooked on admin_init (requires authenticated admin session in WP). Sets a cookie with a fixed value ('1') — no user input stored in cookie value. Low-impact.

negative_findings.area: SQL in PrliLink model (getAll, getOne, create, update, reset, destroy)
negative_findings.reason: All dynamic SQL uses $wpdb->prepare() with typed placeholders (%d, %s), $wpdb->insert(), or $wpdb->update(). The getAll() $where and $order_by parameters receive pre-prepared strings (output of $wpdb->prepare()) from callers, or hardcoded ORDER BY clauses. No raw user input reaches SQL without parameterization.

$sort_str used in ORDER BY clause at line 86 only for whitelisted values (ip, vuid, btype, bversion, host, referer, uri) via switch/case. Default branch uses safe hardcoded value. Any unrecognized input falls to default. Whitelist approach prevents ORDER BY injection.

Protected by secret bookmarklet_auth key ($prli_options->bookmarklet_auth) compared against $_GET['k'] before any link creation. target_url validated with PrliUtils::is_url() and sanitized with esc_url_raw() restricting to http/https schemes.

$service_account_name from get_option('prli_stripe_service_account_name') is unescaped in printf() at line 70. However, value is stored with sanitize_text_field() which strips all HTML tags at write-time (PrliStripeConnectController.php:157). Data source is the Stripe Connect service response, not direct user input. Even if an attacker could manipulate the service response, sanitize_text_field() strips tags before storage. Residual XSS risk requires compromising the Stripe Connect service — out of scope for plugin vulnerability.

wp_verify_nonce at line 15 with explicit check (dies on failure). IR anom_8 flags missing capability — reviewing the actual file, a nonce is present and verified. The action only dismisses a UI notice. Low impact.

out_of_scope.reason: Callbacks unresolved by IR extractor. These belong to the vendored mothership library and are not part of the core plugin surface being reviewed. Would require separate analysis of that vendor library.
out_of_scope.recommendation: Review vendored caseproof/ground-level-mothership AddonsManager separately if in scope.

out_of_scope.reason: Loose comparisons (==, !=, in_array without strict) are a systemic pattern across the codebase. Without a specific exploitable authentication bypass or type juggling chain, these are informational-only. None reached a security boundary with a clear exploit path during this review.
out_of_scope.recommendation: Review any loose comparisons that gate capability or nonce checks specifically.

analysis_notes.ir_extractor_accuracy: The IR extractor produced 33 anomalies. All 33 were refuted as false positives after manual source code verification. The extractor's 'flawed nonce' detection (rule_03) consistently mis-categorized check_ajax_referer($die=false) patterns where the return value is explicitly checked — these are functionally equivalent to $die=true when the calling code tests the return value. The 'guard after side-effect' detection (rules referenced in guard notes) mis-identified initial isset()/$_POST validation checks as side-effects.
analysis_notes.methodology: For each anomaly: (1) located exact source, (2) traced guard execution order, (3) verified all guards precede dangerous operations, (4) confirmed guard return values are tested where $die=false was used, (5) checked capability check depth (some checks are in helper methods not visible at call site).
analysis_notes.coverage: Analyzed: PrliAddonsController, PrliLinksController, PrliPostsController, PrliStripeController, PrliStripeConnectController, PrliAuthenticatorController, PrliOnboardingController, PrliAppController, PrliUpdateController, PrliClicksController, PrliToolsController, PrliPopupController, PrliLink model, PrliClicksHelper. SQL sinks in PrliLink.php, PrliClick.php verified safe.
